I hear that you strongly disagree with my preference, and I respect that you have a different style that works well for you. But calling one style "objectively better" doesn't make sense here—this is a personal preference, not a factual claim. My way of connecting through deep, focused conversations isn't boring or unproductive to me; it's how I feel most engaged and fulfilled.

I don't think either of us needs to change our preferences to match the other. We could even try a mix sometimes, if you're open to it—maybe pick a core topic but let it branch naturally if that feels right, or switch between a couple related subjects. But pressuring me to adopt your style as "better" doesn't help us connect. What do you value most about jumping between many topics? Maybe understanding that can help us meet in the middle.
